sources.text: Rare AI Lab PI: Aobo Li · Halıcıoğlu Data Science Institute (HDSI) · Department of Physics · UC SAN DIEGO aol002@ucsd.edu Nature is full of Rare Physics Events of interest. To search for them, we must encode nature's message into experimental data with rare event search detector , and then decode them to unlock new physics and propel fundamental scientific understanding forward. My group leverage Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a powerful tool to decipher nature's messages. We're Hiring: Postdoctoral Scholar in Agentic ML Development for Nuclear Physics The Rare AI Lab at UC San Diego (HDSI) is looking for a postdoc to develop agentic AI systems for dark matter and neutrino searches (LEGEND, KamLAND-Zen, XLZD, and a quantum-enabled axion haloscope). The postdoc will build on our agentic ML framework SIDERIUS and can take part in DOE Genesis Mission projects. Apply by: December 15, 2026 for full consideration · Start: between January and April 2027 · Appointment: 2 years, renewable Details & Apply on AcademicJobsOnline My Scientific/programmer profiles: News: We're hiring a postdoc! The Rare AI Lab is recruiting a Postdoctoral Scholar in Agentic ML Development for Nuclear Physics. Apply by December 15, 2026 for full consideration. Details in this Link . Our AutoML agent framework SIDERIUS is now open source! It turns AutoML functions into reusable agent capabilities with budget-aware exploration, and on the TIDMAD dark matter benchmark it reaches a 63.8% valid-model proposal rate vs. 1.6% for a general-purpose Codex agent. Link Research Click here for selected publications Nature Neutrino The "ghost particle" that travel through space at almost the speed of light and pass through ordinary matter almost undetected. Dark Matter Mysterious and elusive, dark matter is postulated to constitute about 85% of the matter in our universe. Particle Physics Experiments The LEGEND Experiment Next-generation NLDBD experiment conducted at the INFN Gran Sasso National Laboratory (LNGS) in Italy, aiming at unambiguous discovery of NLDBD utilizing high purity Germanium detectors. The KamLAND-Zen Experiment The monolithic Xenon liquid scintillator detector experiment, carried out at the Kamioka Observatory in Japan, currently holds the world's most stringent limit in the search for neutrinoless double-beta decay (NLDBD). The XLZD Experiment Next-generation liquid xenon observatory formed by the XENON, LZ, and DARWIN collaborations, using a 60-tonne dual-phase time projection chamber to search for WIMP dark matter, neutrinoless double-beta decay, neutrinos, and other rare processes. AI/ML Research Current funded initiatives apply these research directions through agentic AI, surrogate modeling, foundation models, quantum-sensor denoising, low-latency embedded AI, and Bayesian uncertainty quantification. These efforts include four DOE Genesis Mission Phase I awards, with Aobo Li serving as Lead PI on one project and Co-PI on three others. Learn more . AI Agent develop multi-agent AI system that is keen to the critical need of neutrino and dark matter detection, such as experiment monitoring, event reconsutrction, and physics data analysis. These agent will autonomously conduct research and validate result to produce rigorous scientific result. Surrogate Model building uncertainty aware surrogate model to drastically accelerate expensive GEANT4 simulation. This will drastically reduce the cost for designing the next-generation detector as well as conducting background modeling that was not previously possible. Time Series Analysis uncover faint signals from the dark matter or gravitational wave. These signals are buried within ultra-long time series data from quantum sensor readouts. We aim to develop advanced AI algorithms to decipher these signal from the ample quantum noise. Fast Machine Learning on FPGA develop and deploy AI algorithms onto FPGA chips to unveil partices in detector within a few millisecond Physics KamLAND-Zen With the help of KamNet, KamLAND-Zen 800 yields worlds most stringent limit on the effective Majorana mass and the first search for Majorana neutrino in the inverted ordering region! Majorana Demonstrator The Majorana Demonstrator, a predecessor experiment of LEGEND, recently unveiled its final results in 2023; LEGEND-200 is presently in the initial stages of collecting its first set of physics data. Group Members Principle Investigator Aobo Li (and Group Mascot Lulu) Postdoctoral Scholar Yue Ma Graduate Students Sonata Simonaitis-Boyd HDSI PhD student Lucas Venetoulias HDSI PhD student Zhihao Wang Physics PhD student Akbota Assan HDSI Master Student Anish Patnaik HDSI Master Student Weston Chester HDSI Master Student Undergraduate Students Wing Huang: physics Liuxuhong (Francisco) Zhao: data science Jaden Wu: data science (HDSI) Zhen Wang: applied math Alumini & Visiting Scholar Min Zhong: PhD student, now graduated and working at Citadel Securities Fong Vo: Master student at USC Owen Shi: Master student at Columbia University Ann-Kathrin Shuetz: Postdoctoral Scholar at Lawrence Berkeley National Lab, visited Rare AI Lab in March 2024 Kelly Weerman: PhD student at University of Amsterdam, visited Rare AI Lab in Feb. 2025 Eugene Ku: UCSD undergraduate students worked in Rare AI Lab, currently PhD at Texas A&M Alex Migala: UCSD Physics PhD student, conducted first year research rotation at Rare AI lab Avi Mehta: currently working in industry Brian Liu: currently in Lianhui Qin's group working on AI agent Matthew Segovia: currently in Graduate School of Physics Owen Yang: currently work in industry Sophie Wang: data science Luca Georgescu: physics AI Tutorials Introduction Welcome to this AI/ML tutorial repository, developed during my faculty career. This tutorial series aims to provide interdisciplinary training , specifically designed to help physicists cross disciplinary borders into the world of Artificial Intelligence. No prior AI/ML expertise is needed. We start from zero. During these tutorials, you will have the opportunity to move beyond theory and play with real data derived from cutting-edge physics detectors . You will learn how to build neural network models from scratch using this data. Note: This is a growing repository. We plan to release more physics detector datasets and create additional tutorials in the future. Content Overview Datasets: Seven AI-ready physics datasets, ranging from BASIC (e.g., Majorana Demonstrator, CUORE) through INTERMEDIATE (e.g., EXO-200, NEXT) to ADVANCED (nEXO signal denoising and TIDMAD for dark matter discovery). Tutorials: Covers the essentials ("AI In a Nutshell"), coding cookbooks, using ChatGPT for ML, and two additional Machine Learning Course Series. Suggested Learning Paths The Essential Path (Quick Start): BASIC DATASET → 1. AI In a Nutshell (run Jupyter Notebook) → 3. Using ChatGPT (update Jupyter Notebook) The Full Exploration (Deep Dive): BASIC DATASET → 1. Nutshell → 2. Cookbook → 3. ChatGPT → 4. Practical Series → 5. Bootcamp → ADVANCED DATASET. Physics Datasets AI-ready datasets from neutrinoless double-beta decay (0νββ), neutrino mass, and dark matter experiments, many of them prepared for the 0νββ AI Summer School . Fig 1. Sample Waveforms Majorana Demonstrator Data Release BASIC DATASET High Purity Germanium Detector Signals This dataset contains over 3 million data points derived from the Majorana Demonstrator experiment , which utilizes High Purity Germanium Detectors to search for Neutrinoless Double-Beta Decay. Each data point represents a real time-series waveform generated by the detector. Input Data: 1D Numpy vector with 4000 samples (Time Series). Labels: 4 Binary Classification labels + 1 Energy Regression label. Goal: Train ML models to use the waveform as input to predict the analysis labels. Format: HDF5 (See Tutorial 1 for reading instructions). Download Dataset (Zenodo) Read Description (arXiv) Fig 2. Single-Pulse (top) vs Pile-Up (bottom) Event CUORE Pulse Shape Data Release BASIC DATASET Cryogenic Calorimeter Pulses This dataset contains 10,000 triggered events from the CUORE (Cryogenic Underground Observatory for Rare Events) experiment . Each event is a 10-second waveform sampled at 1 kHz, beginning with a 3-second pretrigger baseline. The dataset is evenly split between clean single-pulse events and pile-up events containing two or more pulses. Input Data: 1D array with 10,000 samples (Waveform), eventId. Labels: 1 Binary Classification label (clean single-pulse: 0, pile-up: 1). 90% of events are labeled for training; 10% are reserved for testing. Goal: Identify pile-up events from the raw waveform. Format: HDF5. Waveforms are raw; normalization parameters are provided to apply during data loading. Download Dataset (Zenodo) Read Description (arXiv) Fig 3. Simulated Two-Electron Event SuperNEMO Simulation Dataset BASIC DATASET Electron Tracking Detector Events Simulated data from the SuperNEMO Demonstrator , a detector that reconstructs individual electron trajectories. It covers four physical processes in the source foil: the 0νββ decay signal in 82 Se, and three backgrounds: two-neutrino double-beta (2νββ) decay in 82 Se and decays of the foil contaminants 208 Tl and 214 Bi. Input Data: Numpy array of reconstructed event features (ev_no, E1, E2, tX, tY, tZ, tR, dY, dZ, theta, phiR, phiS). Labels: 1 Multiclass Classification label (0nubb, 2nubb, Bi214, Tl208). Goal: Separate the 0νββ signal from the three background processes. Format: HDF5. Download Dataset & Description (Zenodo) Fig 4. Waveforms on Wire and APD Channels EXO-200 Public Data Release INTERMEDIATE DATASET Liquid Xenon TPC Multichannel Waveforms A subset of the Th-228 calibration data from the EXO-200 experiment , designed for training and testing AI/ML algorithms. Each event includes raw waveforms from the charge (wire) and light (APD) channels, together with reconstructed quantities such as charge energy, light energy, rotated energy, and charge-cluster information. Input Data: Waveforms (226 channels × 600 timesteps). Labels: Charge_Cluster_Number (Multiclass Classification label). Goal: Predict the number of charge clusters in each event directly from the raw waveforms. Format: HDF5. Download Dataset (Zenodo) Fig 5. Signal vs Background 3D Tracks NEXT Simulation Dataset INTERMEDIATE DATASET High-Pressure Xenon Gas TPC Tracks A simulation of ~650k signal (0νββ) and ~500k background (Bi-214) events in the NEXT detector , a high-pressure gaseous xenon time projection chamber. Each event is a set of voxelized (x, y, z) energy depositions: signal events carry a two-electron signature, while background events show a single electron from a gamma interaction. Input Data: Pandas dataframe with columns event_id, x, y, z, energy (3D point cloud). Labels: 1 Binary Classification label (signal or background). Goal: Distinguish two-electron 0νββ tracks from single-electron background tracks. Format: HDF5. Tip: The full dataset is large. Start with 10% of it ( 0nubb_part_1.tar + Bi_part_1.tar ) before training on everything. Download Dataset (Zenodo) Read Description (arXiv) Fig 6. Noisy Charge Waveforms on One Tile nEXO Charge Readout Simulation ADVANCED DATASET Liquid Xenon TPC Signal Denoising 83.5 million simulated double-beta decay events recorded by the charge collectors of a single-phase liquid xenon TPC, following the approximate design of the nEXO experiment . Charge is collected on tiles of 16 × 16 perpendicular electrode strips, and each event is confined to one tile: 32 channels of 1D charge waveforms over 1377 time steps (0.5 μs each). Every event comes in a clean ("noiseless") and a noisy version, along with its energy in MeV. Input Data: Noisy event waveforms (EArrays, convertible to Numpy and Pandas; code provided). sources.text: Contact Us Give us a call or drop by anytime, we endeavor to answer all inquiries within 24 hours. Find us PO Box 16122 Collins Street West Victoria, Australia Email us info@domain.com / example@domain.com Phone support Phone: + (066) 0760 0260 / + (057) 0760 0560 People Home / People Aobo Li Assistant Professor Email: aol002@ucsd.edu Website Nature is full of incredible physics phenomena that we want to study. Unfortunately, nature doesn’t speak English, so we must encode nature’s message into experimental data and subsequently decode them to unlock new physics and propel fundamental science forward. Aobo Li’s research utilizes ultra-sensitive radiation detectors to probe neutrinos and dark matter. His interests in machine learning spans self-supervised learning, time series analysis, and geometric deep learning. These algorithms have the potential to help extracting as much information as possible from radiation detectors. Aobo Li has earned recognition through several awards, including APS Dissertation Award in Nuclear Physics, Postdoc Award of Research Excellence and MLST Paper Award. Aobo Li is an Assistant Professor with the departments of Halıcıoğlu Data Science Institute and Physics.
